section_title: The Wish You Can't Take Back
connection: Curry Barker's directorial debut is a modern spin on the cursed-wish subgenre — <cite index="1-1">Obsession gives chilling modern relevance to a classic tale of a wish gone wrong</cite>, in the lineage of stories where a magical bargain grants a desire but exacts a monstrous price. The horror engine of the film isn't a monster you can outrun, it's a rule: <cite index="3-1">Bear calls One Wish Willow customer service and learns the wish only ends if he or Nikki dies</cite>. There's no safe word, no refund, no tapping out — <cite index="5-2">Bear wants this to end, but he can't take his wish back</cite>, which turns the whole back half of the movie into a countdown with only one exit.
training_tie_in: That's the exact psychology of a fight you can't stop mid-round: once you've made the wish — signed the contract, walked to the ring, thrown the first jab — there's no customer service line to undo it, only the bell or a body on the canvas. Every session on the bag is training for that same fact: quitting isn't actually available once the thing has started, so the only options left are absorb it or finish it. It's why the grind is unglamorous — nobody wants to be the one who has to go the full distance to make it stop.
